mission_03: Quantum kernel methods use quantum circuits to compute kernel functions for classical machine learning algorithms like SVMs. The quantum feature map encodes classical data into quantum states, and the kernel is the squared overlap (fidelity) between two encoded states: k(x1, x2) = |⟨φ(x1)|φ(x2)⟩|². This implicitly maps data into an exponentially large Hilbert space, potentially creating feature representations that are classically intractable. The quantum kernel can capture complex data correlations through entanglement. In this mission, you implement a quantum feature map that encodes data via RY and RZ rotations with entangling CNOTs, compute the kernel function as state overlap, build the full kernel matrix, train an SVM with the precomputed quantum kernel, and make predictions on new data.
